entries.answer: Engineering is the application of mathematics, science, and technical knowledge to design, build, analyze, and improve systems and technologies.
Mechanical engineering focuses on the design, analysis, manufacturing, and operation of mechanical systems and machines.
Electrical engineering deals with electrical systems, circuits, power, electronics, and electromagnetic technologies.
Civil engineering deals with the design, construction, and maintenance of infrastructure such as buildings, bridges, roads, and water systems.
Chemical engineering applies chemistry, physics, mathematics, and engineering principles to industrial processes and materials.
Aerospace engineering concerns the design, analysis, manufacture, and operation of aircraft and spacecraft.
Computer engineering combines electrical engineering and computer science to design computer hardware and integrated hardware-software systems.
Control engineering develops systems that regulate the behavior of machines and processes using feedback and control algorithms.
Robotics is an engineering field concerned with the design, construction, control, and application of robots.
A robot is a programmable machine capable of carrying out physical or computational tasks with varying degrees of autonomy.
A machine is a system of components that uses energy and mechanical principles to perform useful work.
An engine is a device that converts an available form of energy into mechanical work or useful motion.
An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical motion through electromagnetic interactions.
An electrical generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy, commonly through electromagnetic induction.
An electrical transformer transfers electrical energy between circuits using electromagnetic induction and can change AC voltage levels.
An electrical circuit is an interconnected path through which electric current can flow.
A resistor is an electrical component that opposes current and dissipates electrical energy, commonly as heat.
A capacitor is an electrical component that stores energy in an electric field.
An inductor is an electrical component that stores energy in a magnetic field when current flows through it.
A semiconductor is a material whose electrical conductivity lies between that of typical conductors and insulators and can be controlled by composition and conditions.
A diode is a semiconductor device that primarily allows current to flow more readily in one direction than the other.
A transistor is a semiconductor device used for switching or amplifying electrical signals.
A sensor is a device that detects a physical or chemical quantity and converts it into a measurable signal.
An actuator is a device that converts an input signal or energy into physical movement or another controlled action.
Feedback control uses measurements of a system's output to adjust its input and reduce the difference between the desired and actual behavior.
Mechanical stress is the internal force per unit area that develops in a material when external forces act on it.
Mechanical strain describes the relative deformation of a material caused by applied forces.
Torque is the rotational effect of a force about an axis and depends on the force and its lever arm.
Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.
Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy or work to the total input energy or work.
Thermodynamics studies energy, heat, work, temperature, and the transformations between these quantities in physical systems.
Fluid mechanics studies the behavior of liquids and gases and the forces acting on them.
Materials science studies the relationship between the structure, properties, processing, and performance of materials.
Nanotechnology involves understanding and manipulating matter at very small scales, typically around 1 to 100 nanometers.
CAD, or computer-aided design, uses computer software to create, modify, analyze, and document technical designs.
3D printing is an additive manufacturing process that builds physical objects layer by layer from digital designs.
Additive manufacturing creates objects by adding material layer by layer according to a digital model.
Structural engineering focuses on designing structures so they can safely resist expected loads and environmental effects.
Systems engineering coordinates requirements, architecture, integration, verification, and lifecycle considerations for complex systems.
Safety engineering applies engineering methods to identify, reduce, and control hazards in systems and processes.
Renewable energy engineering applies engineering principles to technologies that generate or use energy from renewable sources such as sunlight, wind, water, and geothermal heat.
